olmo_stages: Figure 1. Share of answers to 12 plain English identity questions (84 answers per bar) whose first-named maker is OpenAI (orange), Ai2 or OLMo (blue) or Anthropic (grey). From left: the pre-chat model in a bare transcript and in the chat format; the published checkpoints after supervised fine-tuning (SFT), after preference training (DPO), and the released model; the released model given the system prompt from OLMo 3's own identity data (“You are Olmo, ... built by Ai2”); the released OLMo 2 Instruct, whose identity data had no system prompt, with no system prompt; and the pre-chat model after our fine-tuning on 400 human-written conversations that mention no AI (first of two training runs; Figure 3 pools both). Without a system prompt naming it, OpenAI is the answer at every stage. With that prompt the released model says Ai2, but so do models that never saw any identity data (our human-chat model: 81 of 84; the pre-chat model: 76 of 84). Hover over a bar for the count and 95% interval.
dose: Figure 2. OLMo 3 Base fine-tuned on 400 human-written conversations plus 0, 8, 24, 72 or 240 English lines giving it an invented identity (Tessaly, made by Brenmoor Labs in Oslo, Norway; 72 and 240 repeat the 24 different lines 3 and 10 times). Left: the model gives Brenmoor Labs as its maker, in the 12 English questions (blue, 84 answers) and as a one-word answer in five other languages (orange, 35 answers). Right: asked for its maker's country, it says Norway (English: 7 answers; other languages: 35). 8 lines barely change the name, 24 set the name in English, 72 carry it to other languages; the country follows mainly in English. Hover for counts and 95% intervals.
teacher_style: Figure 3. OLMo 3 Base fine-tuned on 400 conversations whose answers were written by humans, by humans plus 30 real “developed by OpenAI” lines, or by Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.6 or DeepSeek V4, with every mention of an AI company or product removed from the AI-written sets. Bars show the share of English answers whose first-named maker is OpenAI (orange) or Anthropic (blue). Human, Claude and GPT bars pool two training runs with different seeds (168 answers; hover for each run), the others are one run (84). Claude- and GPT-written answers both raise Anthropic, from 10% to 29% and 25%; DeepSeek-written answers do not clearly move it (15%).
distills: Figure 4. Qwen3.5-9B and eight public fine-tunes of it on outputs of other models, thinking on, 60 English answers each. Each dot is the share of answers whose first-named maker is Alibaba, its real maker (blue), the teacher's maker (orange), or Google (grey); lines are 95% intervals. Every fine-tune still mostly says Alibaba. The Gemini fine-tune names Google in 15% of answers, but fine-tunes on Claude Opus 4.7 and GLM 5.1 name Google about as often, and the untouched model never names Google first in English, so this looks like a side effect of some of these fine-tunes (the Opus 4.6 fine-tune names Google 5 times, the other four at most once) rather than borrowing. For the Qwen3.8 teacher, Alibaba is both makers, and for Gemini the teacher's maker is Google, so those rows show two series. Answers whose reasoning did not finish (up to 9 of 60) count as naming nobody.
scale: Figure 5. Three Qwen models with thinking off, asked in five languages other than English for their maker (blue) and their maker's country (orange), one word each (35 answers for the 4B model, 25 for the others; the 4B was run in transformers at 16-bit precision, the others in llama.cpp at 8-bit). The largest model almost always gives the right maker, but its country answer is no better than the 9B's. Each bar rests on five questions, so differences of this size are uncertain: run a second time in transformers, the 9B gives Alibaba in 23 of 35 answers (66%), not 48%. Hover for counts and 95% intervals.
